config.title: Build order placement API with validation

intro.title: Build order placement API with validation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple order placement API endpoint using Node.js and Express. You'll learn how to validate incoming order data, such as checking for required fields and ensuring correct data types, to prevent errors and improve security. The core programming concept is input validation, which is essential for handling user data safely in web applications. You'll use JavaScript, Express middleware, and basic HTTP methods to create a POST endpoint that accepts and validates order details. By the end, you'll have a functional API that can receive order requests and respond with appropriate validation messages.
intro.usecase: Order placement APIs with validation are fundamental to e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Shopify, where customers submit purchase requests that must be validated before processing. In financial applications such as Robinhood or Coinbase, these APIs ensure trade orders meet regulatory requirements and account limits before execution. Restaurant delivery apps like DoorDash use similar validation to confirm order details, pricing, and availability before charging customers. Developers implementing these APIs prevent invalid data from reaching business logic, reducing errors and improving system reliability.

objectives: Construct an Express.js route handler for processing order placement requests
Implement validation middleware to check required order fields and data types
Configure error handling to return appropriate HTTP status codes for invalid requests
Initialize a data structure to store and manage incoming order information
Manipulate request data to format and prepare orders for processing
Integrate validation rules with route handlers to ensure data integrity
Apply conditional logic to validate order quantities and pricing constraints

steps.title: Import Express and required middleware
steps.instruction: Import Express and the body-parser middleware to handle JSON requests in your Node.js application.
steps.hint: Use the 'require' statement to import both Express and body-parser. Remember to assign them to variables.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your code will have the necessary imports to set up an Express server with JSON parsing capabilities.
successCriteria: Express and body-parser are imported using require statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported both Express and body-parser using require statements.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both Express and body-parser to handle JSON requests in your API.

steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance and assign it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use the Express function you imported to create an instance of the Express application.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an Express app instance
const app = express();

steps.title: Configure middleware for JSON parsing
steps.instruction: Configure your Express app to use the built-in JSON middleware to parse incoming JSON request bodies.
steps.hint: Use the app.use() method with express.json() middleware.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding middleware to parse JSON
app.use(express.json());
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will be able to parse JSON data from incoming requests.
successCriteria: The app.use() method is called with express.json() middleware.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.use() with express.json() middleware.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to configure middleware to parse JSON requests using app.use(express.json()).

steps.title: Define order validation function
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateOrder that takes an order object as a parameter and returns true if the order is valid, false otherwise. For now, implement basic validation: check that the order object exists and has a 'total' property that is a number greater than 0.
steps.hint: Define a function with the signature validateOrder(order) that returns a boolean. Inside, check if order exists and if order.total is a number greater than 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateOrder function is created that validates the existence of an order and its total property.
successCriteria: The validateOrder function is defined, accepts an order parameter, and returns true only when order exists and order.total is a number greater than 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it checks both that order exists and that order.total is a number greater than 0 before returning true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation function is missing or doesn't correctly check the required conditions. Remember to validate that order exists and order.total is a positive number.

steps.title: Create POST route for order placement
steps.instruction: Define a POST route at '/api/orders' that handles incoming order placement requests. The route should accept a request and response object.
steps.hint: Use app.post() to define a POST route. The first argument is the path '/api/orders', and the second is a callback function with (req, res) parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route at '/api/orders' is defined and ready to handle order placement requests.
successCriteria: The code includes app.post('/api/orders', (req, res) => {}) with a callback function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.post() with the correct path '/api/orders' and a callback function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST route isn't defined correctly. Check the syntax and ensure you're using app.post().

steps.title: Add validation to order route
steps.instruction: Inside your POST route handler, call the validateOrder function with the request body and handle validation errors by returning a 400 status with an error message.
steps.hint: After receiving the order data, call validateOrder and check if it returns an error. If there's an error, use res.status(400).json() to send the error response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The POST route will now validate incoming order data and return appropriate error responses when validation fails.
successCriteria: The POST route handler calls validateOrder with req.body and returns a 400 status with an error message when validation fails.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling validateOrder with req.body and returning a 400 status with the error message when validation fails.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation isn't properly integrated. Remember to call validateOrder inside the route handler and return a 400 response with the error message when validation fails.

steps.title: Implement successful order response
steps.instruction: Inside the POST route handler, after calling validateOrder, add logic to return a 201 status code with a success message and the order details when validation passes.
steps.hint: Use res.status(201).json() to send a JSON response with a success message and the order object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route should now respond with a 201 status and JSON containing a success message and the order data when validation passes.
successCriteria: The POST route returns a 201 status code with a JSON object containing a 'message' property and the order data when validation is successful.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include both the status code (201) and the JSON response with a message and order data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The successful response logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to use res.status(201).json() with a success message and the order object.

steps.title: Add error handling middleware
steps.instruction: Create an error handling middleware function that catches validation errors and sends a 400 status response with the error message.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes four parameters: error, req, res, and next. Inside, check if the error is a validation error and respond with status 400 and the error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A middleware function is defined that will handle validation errors by sending a 400 response with the error message.
successCriteria: An error handling middleware function is created with four parameters and sends a 400 status response for validation errors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the error handling middleware, but make sure it has all four parameters (error, req, res, next) and sends a 400 response with the error message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling middleware is missing or incorrect. Create a function that takes four parameters and handles validation errors by sending a 400 response.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on port 3000 and log a message to the console when the server is running.
steps.hint: Use app.listen(port, callback) to start the server. The callback function should log a message like 'Server running on port 3000'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be started and accessible on port 3000, with a confirmation message logged to the console.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a server status message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a callback function that logs a message when the server is ready.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server hasn't been started correctly. Use app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback that logs a status message.

steps.title: Test the order placement API
steps.instruction: Add a test case to verify the API responds correctly with valid order data.
steps.hint: Create a test object with valid properties and use console.log to simulate a successful response.

successCriteria: A test order object with items and customerName properties is defined and logged to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
